awaiting: Phase-1 external adversarial coverage audit on an independent 2K polyurethane lacquer dataset (non-Purformance)

Phase-1 wet-lab validation of the intervals: measure scratch hardness on N≥20 formulations sampled from the intervals' near-boundary region and verify empirical coverage matches the KPI marginal coverage within ±5%
capability: Distribution-free calibrated prediction intervals for real experimental coating scratch hardness (Erichsen 435 nano-scratch, Purformance HTE dataset, N=86 2K-polyurethane lacquer formulations). Implements the jackknife+ conformal prediction algorithm (Barber, Candès, Ramdas, Tibshirani 2021 Ann. Statist. 49 (1): 486-507) nested inside three-fold leave-one-iteration-out cross-validation. Emits α∈{0.10, 0.20} prediction intervals with empirically-measured marginal coverage on real held-out DoE iterations. Grants no scoring, batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, or optimizer authority.

fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.prediction_rule: For a new formulation x: compute {ŷ_-i(x)}_{i=1..n_tr} on n_tr leave-one-out refits; return interval [Q_α^-({ŷ_-i(x) - R_i}), Q_{1-α}^+({ŷ_-i(x) + R_i})] where R_i = |y_i - ŷ_-i(x_i)| and Q_α^- = ⌊α(n_tr+1)⌋-th smallest, Q_{1-α}^+ = ⌈(1-α)(n_tr+1)⌉-th smallest. The marginal coverage under exchangeability is ≥ 1 - 2α (Barber et al 2021 Theorem 4.1).

metrics.name: marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_worst_case_floor
metrics.note: Fraction of held-out formulations whose observed scratch hardness falls inside the jackknife+ prediction interval at nominal miscoverage α=0.10. Worst-case coverage floor 1 - 2α = 0.80 is guaranteed under exchangeability by Barber, Candès, Ramdas, Tibshirani 2021 Theorem 4.1. Observed on 86 real Purformance HTE 2K-polyurethane lacquer formulations pooled across three leave-one-iteration-out held-out DoE iterations.

metrics.name: marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_typical_target
metrics.note: Typical target 1 - α = 0.90 (not a proven bound, but the value the coverage guarantee usually achieves under exchangeability). Meeting this stronger target is evidence the exchangeability assumption is not violated by the LOIO iteration structure.

metrics.name: marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_020_meets_worst_case_floor
metrics.note: Same worst-case guarantee at nominal miscoverage α=0.20 (target 0.60). Provides a second alpha level to verify the guarantee is not an artifact of a specific miscoverage.

metrics.name: hostile_null_shuffle_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_worst_case_floor
metrics.note: y-values shuffled with np.random.default_rng(0); features and iteration blocking preserved; jackknife+ intervals recomputed at α=0.10. Coverage guarantee is derived from exchangeability only and should therefore be preserved when y is exchangeably shuffled. This is a direct empirical falsification test of the coverage claim.

metrics.name: hostile_null_width_inflates_over_real_signal
metrics.note: Ratio of hostile-null median interval width to real-signal median interval width (both at α=0.10). Under a shuffled y the base learner cannot fit any signal so residuals must inflate, expanding the conformal intervals. A ratio > 1 is direct quantitative evidence the model has extracted real signal beyond the coverage guarantee alone; the guarantee alone would produce identical widths in both regimes.

metrics.name: worst_per_iteration_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_conditional_floor
metrics.note: Minimum per-iteration coverage across the three LOIO held-out folds at α=0.10. Per-iteration (conditional) coverage is NOT theoretically guaranteed by jackknife+; a low value would flag a fold with catastrophic distribution shift. We report the minimum here as an early-warning indicator, with an intentionally permissive floor because the theoretical guarantee is marginal only.

metrics.name: conformal_tighter_than_parametric_at_alpha_010
metrics.note: Observational (not a gate). At α=0.10 the parametric ±1.96·RMSE_train interval is much narrower than the jackknife+ interval (1.04 N vs 7.31 N median). But the parametric interval also undercovers dramatically (73%, well below the 90% target), which is precisely why distribution-free intervals are the correct methodology on this dataset. Reported to make the trade-off visible: coverage guarantee comes at the cost of wider intervals when the base learner's residual distribution is heavy-tailed.

population: Purformance HTE 2K polyurethane lacquer formulations (Cordts et al., Chem. Mater. 2024, Zenodo 13742098). 86 formulations across three sequential DoE iterations (iteration_1: n=17, iteration_2: n=27, iteration_3: n=42). Target: Kratzhärte (scratch hardness, N, mean 14.7, std 3.0). Features: Vernetzung (crosslinking density), HDI-IPDI ratio, Mattierungsmittel (matting agent), Pigmentpaste — 4 real formulation variables all normalized [0,1]. Hostile-null: same features and iteration blocking, y values shuffled with np.random.default_rng(0).
split_methodology: Nested LOIO×jackknife+. Outer: leave-one-iteration-out (3 folds). Inner: leave-one-out on the training data for jackknife+ residuals. For each outer fold, fit HistGradientBoostingRegressor n_train times (each holding out one training point), record absolute residual on that point, then evaluate the jackknife+ prediction interval on every point in the held-out iteration. Total ~774 fits per full run (69+59+44 inner × 3 outer × 2 alphas / 2 shared + hostile-null). No refitting on the test data; base-learner hyperparameters and random seed exactly match the parent scratch-hardness receipt so point predictions are bit-identical.
theory: Vovk, Gammerman, Shafer 2005 'Algorithmic Learning in a Random World' Springer — foundational conformal prediction
Papadopoulos, Proedrou, Vovk, Gammerman 2002 'Inductive Confidence Machines for Regression' — split conformal for regression
Barber, Candès, Ramdas, Tibshirani 2021 'Predictive inference with the jackknife+' Ann. Statist. 49 (1): 486-507 — jackknife+ construction and 1-2α worst-case coverage bound (Theorem 4.1)
Lei, G'Sell, Rinaldo, Tibshirani, Wasserman 2018 'Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression' JASA 113 (523): 1094-1111
Angelopoulos & Bates 2021 'A Gentle Introduction to Conformal Prediction and Distribution-Free Uncertainty Quantification' arXiv:2107.07511
Cordts, Sassmannshausen, Rendel, Klein, Reddemann, Berge 2024 'High-Throughput and Explainable Machine Learning for Lacquer Formulations' Chem. Mater. — dataset origin, DoE iteration structure
Erichsen 435 nano-scratch method — target measurement standard
Ke, Meng, Finley, Wang, Chen, Ma, Ye, Liu 2017 LightGBM NeurIPS — histogram gradient boosting family (sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor is a compatible re-implementation)
